sections.title: Vehicle identity
paragraphs: The Pegassi Osiris is a two-seat Super-class hypercar. Its low body and upward-opening doors distinguish it from ordinary Los Santos traffic. GTA Wiki records it in both GTA V and GTA Online; this dossier covers Story Mode only.

sections.title: How to obtain
paragraphs: Rockstar’s historical notes specify Legendary Motorsport purchases for PS4, Xbox One and PC; PS3/Xbox 360 used vehicle-storage delivery. The community reference lists a Story price of $1,950,000. Check the in-game listing and your edition before spending; an Online event prize is a different acquisition route.

sections.title: Handling and upgrades
paragraphs: The community vehicle article describes all-wheel drive and notes that suspension upgrades are unavailable at Los Santos Customs. These are reference descriptions, not GameBreak lap tests. Avoid comparing an advertised speed bar with another site’s measured maximum speed as if they were the same measurement.

sections.title: Driving practice
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: use a familiar road loop to compare braking before a bend, corner exit and recovery after a collision. Keep the same character, weather and upgrade state. Photograph the car from the side and inside the cockpit, then label those images with the platform instead of presenting an Online race clip as Story evidence.

sections.title: Scope and saved vehicles
paragraphs: The dossier does not promise insurance, mechanic delivery or Online discounts in single-player. Before experimenting, keep a separate manual save and read your Story garage instructions. Current prices, vehicle persistence and performance have not been playtested on your installed build.

sections.title: Which Virgo?
paragraphs: This entry is the Albany Virgo added to GTA V. It is a two-seat Muscle-class car with rear-wheel drive. Do not substitute the similarly named Virgo Classic or Virgo Classic Custom: a matching word in a search result does not identify the same vehicle.

sections.title: Story Mode purchase
paragraphs: Rockstar lists the Virgo among Update 1.27’s Legendary Motorsport additions. GTABase records a Story Mode purchase price of $195,000. Confirm the vehicle name and current in-game price; the same reference page also contains Online-only purchase, sale and delivery information.

sections.title: Driving characteristics
paragraphs: Its rear-wheel-drive layout is a useful contrast to an all-wheel-drive supercar. GameBreak practice suggestion: compare gentle and abrupt acceleration leaving one corner, then repeat with the same upgrades. A vehicle’s class is a catalogue category; it does not guarantee a competitive result on every route.

sections.title: A collection and photo subject
paragraphs: For a Story collection, record manufacturer, paint, wheels and garage location together. Take one side view for body shape and one front view for the grille. A before/after customization pair is more informative than repeating a promotional cover image, and it makes accidental variant substitutions easier to spot.

sections.title: Avoid Online-only assumptions
paragraphs: No current Story speed test is supplied here. Online resale percentages, special event discounts and delivery services are outside this entry’s scope. Save before buying or changing a collection vehicle, and treat any numerical comparison without an edition and test method as incomplete.

sections.title: Classic coupe identity
paragraphs: The Benefactor Stirling GT is a two-seat Sports Classics coupe. Gull-wing doors and its long front body give it a different visual identity from the Osiris, even though both were included in the same content update. The name is a vehicle model, not a separate racing activity.

sections.title: Find the correct Story listing
paragraphs: The Story reference price is $975,000 at Legendary Motorsport. Rockstar’s notes distinguish the PS4/Xbox One/PC purchase route from the older PS3/Xbox 360 garage delivery. Check your actual edition and available garage before purchasing rather than following an Online showroom event.

sections.title: Customization boundaries
paragraphs: GTA Wiki separates GTA V and Online modification columns. Its HSW upgrade column is unavailable for GTA V Story Mode. Use the Story column when budgeting brakes, engine, exhaust or appearance changes; an HSW performance demonstration cannot establish this Story car’s speed.

sections.title: Make a useful comparison
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: photograph the door open and closed, then run the same short road section before and after one upgrade. Note braking point, camera view and whether traffic interfered. This produces an understandable vehicle showcase without inventing a lap record or claiming a visual modification adds performance.

sections.title: Historical and current information
paragraphs: Community galleries contain Online cargo variants and later liveries. Label those images rather than assuming every pictured option exists in Story Mode. This source review confirms identity and documented availability; it does not verify your save, upgrade prices or present-day handling.
